# Managing Trans Heat Under High Load

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Shift into lower gear to keep RPM above 2500 and back off throttle when ATF temperatures approach limits. [t25]

## Specifications

- **Converter nominal stall speed**: ~2500 rpm [t25] ([Partial] [Unverified] single report)
- **Optimal highway driving range**: 45-70 mph [t25] ([Partial] [Unverified] single report)

## Tips & gotchas

- Use a lower gear to minimize torque converter slip and generated heat. [t25]
- Aim for 190F as a conservative target temperature when easing off the throttle during off-road driving. [t25]

- **t25**: jeff_redx, "Thoughts and Observations on Engine and Auto Trans Cooling", 2008-12-28. https://www.thenewx.org/threads/thoughts-and-observations-on-engine-and-auto-trans-cooling.65980/
